The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran congratulates the people and government of Iraq on the withdrawal of the US occupation forces and other foreign forces from Iraq after two decades of a disastrous military presence in the country, and considers this development a very important and necessary step toward consolidating Iraq’s national sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independence. The tragedy of the 23-year military presence of the United States and its allies in Iraq, which followed the US military invasion of the country on March 20, 2003, under the false pretext of confronting “weapons of mass destruction,” had irreparable consequences for Iraq and the entire region. These included the killing and slaughter of more than one million Iraqis, including tens of thousands of innocent women and children; material losses amounting to hundreds of billions of dollars to Iraq’s physical, security, and governmental infrastructure; the destruction of the environment; and heinous war crimes such as the torture of Iraqi men and women at Abu Ghraib prison, as well as laying the groundwork for Takfiri terrorism and Daesh in Iraq and the surrounding region. The Islamic Republic of Iran, while paying tribute to the resistance and steadfastness of the Iraqi people in the face of occupation, terrorism, and sectarianism, stresses the need to respect Iraq’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity and notes that the military presence of the United States and its allies in the countries of the region has produced no result other than promoting violence, insecurity, division, and terrorism. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, while commemorating the memory of the hundreds of thousands of martyrs who lost their lives in the struggle against occupation and terrorism, particularly Martyrs Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis and Hajj Qassem Soleimani, stresses the need to hold the US government accountable and bring it to justice for the crimes committed and the losses inflicted on the people of Iraq and other countries throughout the period of occupation.

Following baseless allegations made by the British prime minister against the Islamic Republic of Iran, Hugo Shorter, the British ambassador to Tehran, was summoned by Majid Takht-Ravanchi, Deputy Foreign Minister for Political Affairs, and Iran’s strong protest over the continuation of the British government’s destructive approach toward Iran was conveyed to him. During the summons, the Iranian deputy foreign minister, recalling the British government’s international responsibility for its numerous wrongful acts against the Iranian people, particularly its provision of military bases and facilities under British jurisdiction for the preparation and execution of the US-Zionist military aggression against Iran, stressed: “The recent propaganda campaign by the British government, which has leveled a baseless accusation under the pretext of an alleged attempt to carry out sabotage at the Fairford base, can in no way overshadow Britain’s complicity in the military aggression against the Iranian people, and the British government must be held accountable for its participation in the crime of aggression and war crimes committed by the United States and the Zionist regime.” Takht-Ravanchi rejected the baseless and frivolous claim by British officials linking the alleged sabotage plot at the Fairford military base to Iran, stressing the need for an official explanation by the British government in this regard and for it to rectify its inappropriate approach toward Iran. item.title: Iranian Japanese Foreign Ministers hold phone conversation
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held a phone conversation at noon on Thursday. During the phone conversation, the two sides exchanged views on Tehran-Tokyo bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister elaborated on Iran’s positions and views regarding the situation in the region, stressing that the continued insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf region is solely the result of the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, and that the only way to restore security is to stop the US’s illegal activities. Araghchi also explained the good offices by some mediators to advance the diplomatic process, stressing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to defend its interests. The Japanese Foreign Minister, for his part, elaborated on Japan’s views regarding matters of common interest.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the visit of Benjamin Netanyahu, the child-killing and warmongering prime minister of the Zionist regime, to the United Arab Emirates, and warns of the extremely dangerous consequences of the presence of the occupying regime in the region. At a time when the West Asia region is experiencing one of the most fragile and sensitive periods in its history due to the Zionist regime’s military aggression against Iran and the intensification of its occupation and genocide in Islamic lands, particularly Palestine and Lebanon, the presence of a criminal whose hands are stained with the blood of hundreds of thousands of innocent people and is wanted by international courts is extremely dangerous and alarming. There is no doubt that, given the Zionist regime’s proven hostility and animosity toward Iran and other countries of the region, as well as the regime’s repeated threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran, all countries in the region should be mindful of the consequences and repercussions of such a presence, which poses a threat to the collective peace and security of the region. Regional security is a collective and indivisible matter, and any move that paves the way for the entry of destabilizing actors into the region will ultimately be detrimental to all countries of the region and will lead to further division, as well as increased insecurity and instability in West Asia. Accordingly, regional governments are expected, in recognition of their responsibility toward regional peace and stability, to refrain from providing the grounds for the destructive presence of the Zionist regime and not allow the territories of countries in the region to become a platform for destabilizing actions against other countries of the region.

🔹Today is the last day of our stay in New York. We have had several very busy days in terms of the number of meetings that were held. We had a great many bilateral and multilateral meetings. 🔹The President, whom we had the honor of accompanying, had an intensive schedule, and I, too, had numerous meetings alongside him, both before and after his engagements. We spoke with the media and had extensive discussions with think tanks and members of the think tank community. We met with various countries' officials, as well as officials from the United Nations and other international organizations, and several objectives were pursued throughout all these engagements. 🔹First, it was to ensure that the voice of the Iranian people’s righteousness and their plight was heard by the world, to defend the interests of the Iranian people, and to demonstrate that Iran continues to be present on the international stage with strength and confidence. 🔹We encountered officials from many countries who were interested in engaging in dialogue with Iran, and a very large number of our meetings were held at the request of the other side. It was evident in these meetings that, contrary to what the United States and the Zionist regime tried to portray, the Islamic Republic is by no means isolated; rather, it is highly respected. 🔹It was stated in numerous meetings that both the people and officials of those countries genuinely appreciate what Iran did and the steadfastness it demonstrated in the face of what is ostensibly the world’s largest military. This steadfastness made many countries and many people proud. 🔹Another objective we pursued, which is a very important one, was to convey to the world the country’s positions regarding the war, and particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz. 🔹There are conditions set by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, and these conditions must be fulfilled for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened. Our mission was to convey these conditions both to the American side and to all other countries and the international community, so that they would be aware that Iran has a plan in this regard. Iran’s conditions are entirely fair and logical, and if the Americans claim that they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we present this solution to them. 🔹Our plan, which became known as the seven-point plan, was conveyed to the Americans through the Qatari intermediary. Despite the remarks made by the US president, I said that we were awaiting an official response from the United States through the intermediaries. Today, one of the Qatari intermediaries held another meeting with us. We discussed various issues and exchanged ideas on how to facilitate the fulfillment of Iran’s conditions and how these conditions could be met. They had some ideas, and we discussed them. They are going to raise this matter with the American side once again, and then the American side’s final response will be conveyed to us through the Qatari intermediary. They hope this will be done by tomorrow. 🔹I will fly to Tehran in a few hours, and whenever the Qataris have a response, they know themselves how they can convey it to us. These communications and messages exchanged between the Qatari and Pakistani mediators had already existed. Now, in light of the plan presented by Iran, they have taken on a more serious form. If there is a response, the Qataris will convey it, and a decision will then be made in Tehran based on that response. 🔹We have seen that, over the past few hours, a media campaign has emerged in various outlets, with claims being made and statements attributed to Iran. I categorically state that there has been no change whatsoever in Iran’s positions. Our conditions for reopening the Strait are clear. Our position on other issues is also clear. At present, there has been absolutely no discussion of any flexibility on our part.

🔹Our position is clear. At present, the only issue is the Strait of Hormuz. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is also contingent upon the fulfillment of a number of conditions that we have communicated to the other side. I would ask that no attention be paid to the speculation or deliberate media narratives being created by certain outlets.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mali, on Monday afternoon. During the meeting, the two sides discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Mali bilateral relations and international developments. The Foreign Minister expressed appreciation for Mali’s principled positions in opposition to violations of the law and unilateral coercive measures, as well as for the solidarity expressed by the people and government of Mali with Iran in the face of the military aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime. Emphasizing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to strengthen relations with developing countries, including African countries, particularly the member states of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), the Foreign Minister announced Iran’s readiness to hold a joint meeting with the three member states of the Alliance of Sahel States. Recalling the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position in support of the independence and national sovereignty of all countries, Araghchi condemned the pressures and unlawful interference by certain European countries in the internal affairs of the Sahel countries, which have engaged in creating and financing terrorist groups and organized crime in the region. The Malian Foreign Minister expressed satisfaction with the growing trend in his country’s relations with Iran, outlined recent developments in Mali and the Sahel region, and stressed that his country and other African nations would not allow the colonial and interventionist ambitions of certain European governments to be realized.
